statement.p: Find \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r where C is a circle of radius 1 in the plane x+y+z=2, centered at (1,2,-1) and oriented clockwise when viewed from the origin, if \vec F = -5 z\vec j + 2 y\vec k

static.solution: \mbox{curl }\vec F = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\ \amp \ \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \ \amp \ \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\\ 0 \amp -5 z \amp 2 y \end{array} \right| = 7\vec i, writing S for the disk in the plane enclosed by the circle, Stokes' Theorem gives \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S\mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_S 7\vec i\cdot d\vec A. Now d\vec A=\vec n\, dA, where \vec n is the unit vector perpendicular to the plane, so \vec n = \frac1{\sqrt{3}}(\vec i+\vec j+\vec k). Thus \int_C\vec F\,d\vec r = \int_S 7\vec i\cdot \frac{\vec i+\vec j+\vec k}{\sqrt{3}}\,dA = \int_S\frac{7}{\sqrt{3}}\,dA = \frac{7}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \hbox{Area of disk } = \frac{7}{\sqrt{3}} \pi 1^2=\frac{7\pi}{\sqrt{3}}.
